conclusions: The product of two spectral spaces is spectral.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ and $Y$ are spectral,
\item $f$ is spectral and bijective, and
\item generalizations (resp.\ specializations) lift along $f$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f$ is a homeomorphism.

reason: A bijective spectral map becomes a constructible-topology homeomorphism; lifting of specialization or generalization upgrades it to an ordinary homeomorphism.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
The inverse limit of a directed inverse system of finite sober
topological spaces is a spectral topological space.
conclusions:
The inverse limit of a directed inverse system of finite sober
topological spaces is a spectral topological space.

reason: Inverse images of opens in finite sober stages give compact-open bases; compatible stage generic points prove sobriety of the limit.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $c : X \to X'$ be the canonical continuous map to a sober topological space $X'$ characterized by the universal property that every continuous map $X \to Y$ to a sober topological space $Y$ factors uniquely through $c$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $X$ is quasi-compact, so is $X'$.
\item If $X$ is quasi-compact, has a basis of quasi-compact opens,
and the intersection of two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact, then
$X'$ is spectral.
\item If $X$ is Noetherian, then $X'$ is a Noetherian spectral space.
\end{enumerate}
